Pawmpt

A little pal on your Omarchy desktop that gets things done.

![Pawmpt](preview.png) Pawmpt is a small creature that lives on your desktop. Pick one of ninety characters or bring your own picture, dress it in skins, hats and capes, and click it to ask something. Your question goes to the coding agent you choose, opencode by default, with the model you pick. The pal shows what the agent does while it works and answers in a speech bubble. It can keep the conversation going, work in the folder of the window you are in, read what you selected, and run commands or edit files when you let it. ## Features - **Ninety characters** in eleven categories (Classic, Animals, Anime, Game heroes, Fantasy, Sci-fi, Spooky, Food, Nature, Retro and pixel, Dev and desk), and any PNG, JPG, WebP, SVG or animated GIF of your own. - **A wardrobe**: fifteen skins, your own colors, fills, patterns, outlines, glow, eyes and mouths, twenty-seven things to wear, and whole pals you save under a name. - **Life**: sixteen idle moves, blinking, eyes that follow the mouse, falling asleep, and sixteen ways to move about the screen, from strolling and bouncing to following or running from the mouse. - **An agent that works**: opencode with any model your providers offer, Ollama, or a command of your own, with live progress, tokens and cost, quick actions, follow-ups and voice through Hex. - **Context**: the active window's folder and title, what you selected and what you copied, each one only when you turn it on. - **Settings in the house style**: a bar panel or its own window, a search box over every page, color schemes from your theme or window border, and an About page. ### The agent The bubble shows each step as it happens (› bash: git status, › read: src/main.rs), then the answer. **Reply** continues the chat, **Copy** and **Copy code** copy the answer, **Retry**, **Go on** and **Simpler** ask again, **New chat** starts over, and **Open in opencode** opens the same conversation in a terminal. **Stop** ends a long run. Quick actions (Explain, Summarize, Fix it, Translate, Reply, Shorter, and one of your own) work on what you selected. ### Ask by voice [Hex](https://anoma.ly/hex) turns your voice into text on your own machine. Pawmpt does not listen itself: it tells Hex to start recording and, when you are done, to stop and hand over the words (`hex dictation start` and `hex dictation stop --print`), then asks the agent. 1. Install Hex and set it up once: `curl -fsSL https://anoma.ly/hex/files/install-linux.sh | sh`, then `hex model install`. 2. Settings › Agent › Voice › **Ask by voice** › Hex. 3. Click the mic in the question box, give a click **Ask by voice** (Controls or Bar), or bind `omarchy-shell io.github.qempexe.pawmpt voice` to a key. By default the transcription opens in the question box for review; `voice cancel` throws it away. By default, Hex puts the transcription in the question box for you to review before sending. Turn on **Send when I stop speaking** to send it immediately. **Stop listening after** ends the recording and follows that same choice. **Hex command** is for when Hex is not on the PATH (`~/.local/bin/hex` is tried anyway). If Hex is not running, Pawmpt starts it and tries again. Pawmpt ends only the recording it started: - **Cancel** (`voice cancel`) drops it. Hex 3.3 and later have no cancel, as every dictation there finishes, so Pawmpt stops it with `hex dictation stop --print`, which never pastes, and throws the words away. Hex keeps them in its History as Printed. If Hex can't stop it, Pawmpt says so, and how to stop it yourself. - **Turning voice off, or hiding Pawmpt,** drops it too, so it never keeps recording where you can't see it. A shell reload drops it a moment later. - **A dictation of your own already recording** is left alone: Pawmpt asks you to finish it first instead of taking your words. - **Hex's own shortcut** also finishes a recording Pawmpt started, and Hex then pastes the words where you are, as usual. Pawmpt notices within a few seconds and says so, and it does the same when Hex stops. ### The wardrobe ![The wardrobe](screenshots/wardrobe.png) ### Settings ![Settings, part one](screenshots/settings-1.png) ![Settings, part two](screenshots/settings-2.png) ## Installation ```bash omarchy plugin add https://github.com/qempexe/omarchy-pawmpt.git --enable omarchy restart shell ``` The bar button goes to the right of the bar; move it from the bar settings, or with `omarchy bar move io.github.qempexe.pawmpt --section left` (or `center`, `right`). For the agent, install [opencode](https://opencode.ai) (1.x or 2.x) and connect a provider with `opencode auth login`, or install [Ollama](https://ollama.com), Claude Code or Codex. Asking by voice needs [Hex](https://anoma.ly/hex) (see [Ask by voice](#ask-by-voice)). Everything else comes with Omarchy: `hyprctl`, `wl-clipboard`, `xdg-open` and `python3`, which runs the small bridges in `tools/` that pass Allow and Deny between Pawmpt and opencode, Claude Code or Codex. ## Usage | On the pal | Does | | --- | --- | | Left click | ask something; Enter sends, Esc closes | | Drag | move it; drop it at a screen's side edge to send it to the next screen | | Right click | the menu | | Middle click | the settings | What each click does is yours to change in **Controls**. | On the bar button | Does | | --- | --- | | Left click | show or hide the pal | | Middle click | ask something | | Right click | open Pawmpt | ### From a terminal ```bash omarchy-shell io.github.qempexe.pawmpt toggle # also: show, hide, ask, settings, panel, wardrobe omarchy-shell io.github.qempexe.pawmpt send "summarise my notes" omarchy-shell io.github.qempexe.pawmpt quick explain # a quick action on what you selected omarchy-shell io.github.qempexe.pawmpt voice toggle # also: start, stop, cancel omarchy-shell io.github.qempexe.pawmpt retry # also: newChat omarchy-shell io.github.qempexe.pawmpt character cat # also: nextCharacter, nextSkin, surprise omarchy-shell io.github.qempexe.pawmpt skin Mint omarchy-shell io.github.qempexe.pawmpt wear tophat # also: undress omarchy-shell io.github.qempexe.pawmpt pal "My pal" # a pal you saved omarchy-shell io.github.qempexe.pawmpt status ``` ## Configuration Everything applies at once and is saved in `~/.local/state/omarchy-pawmpt/`. Each changed row gets a **↺** to put it back, and **Reset all** in the header puts back everything. | Page | Setting | Default | | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Pal | Size, Opacity | 88 px, 100% | | | | Shadow, Blink, Eyes follow the mouse | off, on, on | | | | While idle | Breathe | or Bob, Sway, Hop, Still, Wobble, Twirl, Shiver, Float, Dance, Jumpy, Heartbeat, Tilt, Flip, Boing, Drowsy | | | Fall asleep after | never | up to 120 minutes | | | Surprise me | Never | a new look at every start, every hour or every day | | Movement | Moves | Stays put | or strolls, roams, bounces, follows or runs from the mouse, circles, patrols the edges and more | | | Speed, Keep away from the edges | 60 px/s, 0 px | | | | Rest now and then, Face where it goes | on, on | | | | Stop when the mouse is on it, Stop while the agent works | on, on | | | Controls | Left, right and middle click | Ask, Menu, Settings | | | | Drag it around, Remember where it was | on, on | | | | Drop it at the side to change screen | on | | | Agent | Agent | opencode | or Ollama, Claude Code, Codex, or your own command | | | Model | the agent's own default | searchable list of every model your providers offer | | | Agent mode | Build | or Plan, which only reads and suggests | | | Thinking effort | Model default | Low, Medium, High or Max | | | Let it act | off | opencode does everything without asking; off, it reads and searches on its own and asks with Allow once and Deny for anything else | | | Look things up online | off | with Let it act off, lets it search the web and open pages without asking | | | Answer style, Answer in | As it likes, any language | Short, Detailed, Step by step or Simple | | | Remember the conversation | on | a new chat after 45 minutes of quiet | | | Tell it about the active window | on | | | | Tell it what I have selected, what I copied | off, off | at most 4000 characters | | | Work in | The active window's folder | or Home, or a folder | | | Quick actions | on | and one of your own | | | Copy the answer, Notify me | off, off | | | | Give up after, Try again when it fails | 300 s, never | | | | Ask by voice | Off | Hex, with review before sending by default | | Bubble | Width, Text size | 340 px, 13 | | | | Close after, Opens | never, where there is room | | | | Show what it is doing, tokens and folder, follow-up buttons | on, on, on | | | Colors | Colors | Follow theme | Follow theme, Window borders, Custom or Monochrome | | | Custom colors | | background, text and accent, used exactly as you pick them | | Appearance | Row style, Spacing, Roundness, Text size | Soft, Comfortable, 4, 100% | | | Window | Panel width, height | 560 × 680 | | | | Open as | Bar panel | or Own window | | | Window outline, tint, opacity | off, 0, 97 | the outline in your window border's colors | | Bar | Bar button shows | A tiny copy of your pal | or An icon | | | Left, middle and right click | Show or hide, Ask, Open Pawmpt | | **About**, the last page, has the logo, the version and a link to more plugins. Hyprland tiles new windows. To float the popped-out panel, add to `~/.config/hypr/hyprland.lua`: ```lua o.window({ class = "^org\\.quickshell$", title = "^Pawmpt$" }, { tag = "+pawmpt-window" }) o.window({ tag = "pawmpt-window" }, { float = true }) o.window({ tag = "pawmpt-window" }, { center = true }) o.window({ tag = "pawmpt-window" }, { size = { 560, 680 } }) ``` ## Troubleshooting - **The pal doesn't show after installing.** Restart the shell once with `omarchy restart shell`. - **The bar button does nothing.** It looks for Pawmpt's service through the bar, and through Pawmpt itself when the bar is a replacement that can't hand it over. If it still does nothing, restart the shell. - **It keeps thinking.** Check that `opencode run "hi"` answers in a terminal. - **It pauses before an action.** With **Let it act** off, opencode asks first: the bubble shows what it wants to do, with **Allow once** and **Deny**. Turn Let it act on to let it go ahead without asking. - **It asks before searching the web.** With Let it act off, turn on **Look things up online** to let it search without asking. - **opencode didn't start.** Pawmpt starts its own opencode server for each question (`opencode serve` on 127.0.0.1, with a random password), so `opencode serve` has to work in a terminal. - **No models in the list.** Connect a provider with `opencode auth login`, then press **Refresh**. - **Where things live.** | Path | Contents | | --- | --- | | `~/.local/state/omarchy-pawmpt/` | your settings, skins and pals | | `~/.config/pawmpt/characters/` | the characters you added, one folder per category | - **Network.** Pawmpt itself goes nowhere. Your question goes to the agent you picked, which talks to its own provider. - **What it reads.** The active window's title and folder, and what you selected or copied, are only read when you ask, only when that setting is on, and at most 64 KB of it. - **What Let it act off does.** opencode may read files on its own, and search them when no key or password file is in the folder it searches (below). Anything else (a command, an edit, working outside the work folder, another agent, the web unless **Look things up online** is on) waits for **Allow once** or **Deny** in the bubble, and a question back to you is turned down. Keys and passwords (`.env` files, `~/.ssh`, `~/.gnupg`, `~/.password-store`, `~/.aws`, `~/.kube`, `.netrc`, `.git-credentials`, `*.pem`, `*.key`, `.npmrc`, `.pypirc`, the GitHub CLI's `hosts.yml`, `rclone.conf`, the keyrings, and opencode's, Codex's and Claude Code's own sign-in files) can't be read or changed, with Let it act on too, also when the work folder is a git repository with them at its top, such as a home folder kept in git. The rules go to opencode in its environment, after your own config files, and are set for its agents as well, so an `opencode.json` in the work folder can't widen them. Each question gets a private opencode server on 127.0.0.1 with a random password, so the rules hold while opencode's background service runs too. These are opencode's own rules, not an operating system sandbox, and the model provider still gets the question and the context you turned on. - **Searches and keys.** A search reads every file in its folder, hidden ones too, and opencode checks it apart from reading. Searching a single file reads the whole folder the file is in with opencode 1, so that folder is what counts. So every search goes to Pawmpt first, with Let it act on too: it is let through without asking when none of those files is in that folder, and turned down when one is, with a reason, so opencode goes on another way (a search in a folder without them, or reading files one by one). A folder too big for Pawmpt to look through in time asks in the bubble. The language server is checked the same way, by its file. - **Agents that start agents.** The permission requests of an agent opencode starts for a question (general, explore) come to the bubble as well, and its questions back are turned down, so the answer no longer waits on them for ever. - **Project trust.** opencode loads project configuration, plugins and MCP servers from the work folder. Those components run with your user account's access. Use **Work in** with a folder you trust, and review project extensions before running an agent there. Hex and custom agents also run as your user; configure them only with executables you trust. **Let it act** is off by default; turning it on lets opencode act without asking. - **What other users can see.** Your question, the context and the answers never go in a command's arguments, which anyone on the computer can list: the agent gets the question on stdin, copying goes to `wl-copy` on stdin, and a notification only says that an answer is ready. The one exception is putting `{prompt}` in your own command. - **Approval buttons for a custom agent.** Turn on **Approval bridge** only when your command is an adapter for an agent that can pause for permission. Pawmpt uses a JSON Lines request/reply protocol described in [`tools/AGENT_APPROVAL_PROTOCOL.md`](tools/AGENT_APPROVAL_PROTOCOL.md). The adapter must translate Allow or Deny to that agent's own permission API; ordinary `claude -p` or `codex exec` commands do not speak this protocol by themselves. - **Approval buttons for Claude Code and Codex.** Select the named agent in Settings. Pawmpt connects Claude Code's permission-prompt MCP tool or Codex's app-server request channel to the same Allow once / Deny card, with **Allow all this run** beside it. Their own settings can still pre-allow or deny specific actions before they reach Pawmpt. - **Keys and passwords with Claude Code and Codex.** The same files are kept from them. Claude Code gets deny rules for reading and editing them, and Pawmpt turns down any request for one. Codex runs read-only in a permissions profile that can't read them, by a command either (a Codex too old for profiles runs in its plain read-only sandbox, and the bubble says so). A command that names one of those files is always asked on its own, with a warning, and **Allow all this run** never covers it. With opencode and **Let it act** on, such a command still asks. - **What the card shows.** A request is shown as plain text, without control and direction characters, and a long one says how much isn't shown. A click in the first moment after a card appears is ignored, so a card that pops up under your pointer isn't answered by accident. More than twelve requests waiting at once are denied. - **Stopping.** Stop, the time limit, turning the plugin off and a shell restart stop the agent and everything it started. - **Codex desktop apps.** If Codex reports that a requested Strata, Brave, Firefox, Chromium, Foot or Glances launch failed because its sandbox cannot reach the display, Pawmpt offers an Allow once button to start only that app directly in your Omarchy desktop session. It does not retry the Codex turn outside its sandbox. ## Contributing Bug reports and ideas are welcome as [issues](https://github.com/qempexe/omarchy-pawmpt/issues). [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) shows how to add a character, a skin or something to wear, and how to run the checks. Everyone taking part is expected to follow the [code of conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). What changed in each version is in the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md). ### Source layout ``` qml/ ├── Service.qml settings, characters, skins, the agent, voice, ipc ├── Pal.qml the pal on the desktop: moving, the prompt, the bubble, the menu ├── BarWidget.qml the bar button and the panel by the bar ├── Panel.qml the panel that hangs off the bar ├── PopoutWindow.qml the panel as a window of its own ├── UiState.qml colors, spacing and the open page ├── views/ PalView, SettingsView, CharactersPage, SkinsPage, DressPage, PalsPage, AboutPage ├── controls/ Critter (one pal, drawn or a picture), SettingRow, TileArt, Btn, Chip, Field, Sw, Txt, PasteInput └── js/ ├── Schema.js every setting: its page, options and default ├── Skins.js the characters, the skins and the things to wear ├── Draw.js how every character and item is drawn ├── Prompt.js what is sent to the agent ├── Voice.js asking by voice through Hex ├── Theme.js, Glow.js, Registry.js assets/ the logo, light and dark tools/ check.js (every character at every size), gen-manifest.js, preview.js, opencode_bridge.py, claude_bridge.py, codex_bridge.py (Allow and Deny for each agent), bridge_common.py (what they share), AGENT_APPROVAL_PROTOCOL.md (the same for an agent of your own) tests/ node tests/test_manifest.js, test_prompt.js, test_voice.js, test_glow.js, test_bridges.js, python3 tests/test_bridge_common.py ``` ### Upgrading and uninstalling ```bash omarchy plugin update io.github.qempexe.pawmpt omarchy restart shell ``` ```bash omarchy plugin remove io.github.qempexe.pawmpt omarchy restart shell rm -rf ~/.local/state/omarchy-pawmpt ~/.config/pawmpt # settings, pals and your characters, if you want them gone ``` ## License and credits [MIT](LICENSE). - Inspired by **[goop](https://github.com/nightdevil00/mihai.goop)**, the idea of a creature on the desktop that takes requests. - Thanks to the **Omarchy** project for the shell and its plugin system, to **Hyprland**, and to **Quickshell** and **Qt** for the toolkit. - The characters are drawn from scratch and only nod at the kinds of heroes they are named after.

# Changelog

All notable changes to Pawmpt. The format follows
[Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/), and versions follow
[Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/).

## [1.1.3] - 2026-11-12

### Security

- opencode could read `~/.ssh` keys when the work folder is a git repository with them at
  its top, such as a home folder kept in git: opencode matches its rules against the path
  from that top folder, `.ssh/id_ed25519`, which `*/.ssh/*` doesn't match. Every rule is
  now also set without its leading `*/`.
- A search of a single file let through without asking could still read `~/.ssh` keys:
  opencode 1 searches the whole folder a file, or a path that isn't there, is in, so a
  search of `~/.bashrc` searched the home folder. That folder is what Pawmpt looks through
  now, with links followed for the place searched.
- Files with keys and passwords can't be changed by opencode either, with Let it act on
  too: an edit reads the file first.

## [1.1.2] - 2026-11-12

### Security

- opencode could read a file that holds keys or passwords through a search: a search
  reads every file under its folder, hidden ones too, and opencode checks it apart from
  reading, so the rules that keep those files from being read didn't cover it. With the
  home folder as the work folder, a search could return `~/.ssh` keys, and in a project
  the lines of its `.env` files, without asking. Every search now goes to Pawmpt first,
  with Let it act on too: it is let through when none of those files is in its folder and
  turned down, with a reason, when one is. A folder too big to look through in time asks.
  The language server is checked the same way, by its file.
- The rules are set for the agents opencode starts (general, explore) as well, so an
  `opencode.json` in the work folder can't widen them there.

### Fixed

- A permission request from an agent that opencode started for a question was never
  shown, and the answer waited for ever. Those requests come to the bubble now, and
  questions back from them are turned down.

## [1.1.1] - 2026-11-11

### Security

- Claude Code can no longer read the files that hold keys and passwords: it gets deny rules
  for them, and Pawmpt turns down any request for one. In 1.1.0 it could read a `.env` file
  in the work folder without asking.
- Codex runs in a permissions profile that can't read those files, by a command either. In
  1.1.0 an approved command could read `~/.ssh`.
- A command that names one of those files is always asked on its own, with a warning.
  **Allow all this run** never covers it, and with opencode it asks with **Let it act** on too.
- More files are kept out of reach: `.npmrc`, `.pypirc`, the GitHub CLI's `hosts.yml`,
  `rclone.conf`, the keyrings, and Codex's and Claude Code's own sign-in files.
- The approval card shows a request as plain text without control and direction characters,
  says how much of a long one isn't shown, and ignores a click in the first moment after it
  appears. More than twelve requests waiting at once are denied.
- A request that can't reach Pawmpt is denied, and a reply for a request that wasn't asked is
  ignored.

### Fixed

- opencode 1.x works again; 1.1.0 stopped with "server did not become ready".
- An opencode answer is no longer cut short while a permission card is open or the model is
  slow, and "Agent action" lines no longer show up in it.
- A second Allow or Deny sent right after the first is no longer lost.
- Stop, the time limit, turning the plugin off and a shell restart stop the agent and
  everything it started. Before, the bridge could wait forever and leave `opencode serve`,
  Claude Code or Codex running.
- Claude Code shows its steps and its answer as they come, and the tokens and cost under it.
- Codex shows its steps and the tokens, and says so when it stops before answering.
- A missing agent says which one to install instead of failing silently.
- The About tab shows the right version.

## [1.1.0] - 2026-11-08

### Added

- OpenCode permission requests now appear in Pawmpt with Allow once and Deny buttons.
- Native Claude Code and Codex adapters route their permission requests through Pawmpt.
- Custom agents can use the documented JSON Lines approval bridge.
- Codex can ask before starting an allowlisted desktop app when its sandbox cannot reach
  the display; it does not rerun the agent outside its sandbox.

### Changed

- Hex dictation now goes to the question box for review before sending by default.
- Selected text, clipboard contents, window context and prior answers are tagged as
  untrusted reference data in the composed prompt. Direct questions are normalized and
  length-limited before they are sent.
- OpenCode's **Let it act** setting now uses its permission prompts when off and automatic
  approval when on. The documentation describes these as app-level permissions, not an OS
  sandbox.

## [1.0.6] - 2026-11-06

### Security

- Cancel works on Hex 3.3, which has no `hex dictation cancel`: the recording went on
  after Cancel, with Pawmpt idle. It is now stopped with `hex dictation stop --print`,
  which never pastes, and the words are thrown away. A Hex with cancel still uses it.
- A drop that fails is no longer ignored: Pawmpt says Hex may still be recording, and how
  to stop it.
- Only a recording Pawmpt may have started is dropped. Cancel while transcribing, or
  before a start could reach Hex, drops nothing, so it can't end a dictation of your own.
- A dictation of your own that is already recording is left alone, instead of Pawmpt
  taking it over and asking the agent with your words.
- Turning voice off, or hiding Pawmpt, drops the recording, so it never goes on where you
  can't see it.
- While listening, Pawmpt notices when Hex's shortcut ends the recording (Hex then pastes
  the words where you are) or when Hex stops, and says so instead of showing it listens.

### Fixed

- Starting voice while the last recording is still being stopped says so, instead of
  doing nothing.
- Stopping and dropping a recording use the Hex command it was started with, even if the
  setting changed in between.

## [1.0.5] - 2026-11-06

### Security

- Cancel while voice was starting could still leave Hex's first `hex dictation start`
  running: it was a child of the step Pawmpt stopped, and outlived it. If it was slow to
  get through, it could begin recording after the cancel, with Pawmpt idle. Each step of
  starting to record is now its own process, and that process is hex itself, so stopping
  a step stops hex, and Hex is told to cancel only once it is gone.
- When the shell reloads while asking by voice, Hex is told to cancel a moment later, in
  case the step that was running got the start through.

## [1.0.4] - 2026-11-06

### Security

- Cancelling voice while Hex was still starting up could let that start begin recording
  afterwards, with Pawmpt idle and not counting down to stop it. Cancel now stops the
  pending start, and Hex is told to cancel only once that start is gone, so nothing is
  left recording. Voice can't be started again until the cancel is done.
- Pawmpt's settings and characters folders are made private again at every start, also
  when they are left over from an older version with looser permissions.

## [1.0.3] - 2026-11-05

### Security

- **Let it act** off passes restrictive opencode permission rules and starts a private
  server for each run. These are app-level rules, not an operating system sandbox; they
  cannot guarantee isolation from extensions, MCP servers, provider behavior, or changes
  in opencode.
- The rules deny common credential paths and file types, editing, command execution and
  network tools by default. Pattern matching is best effort and cannot guarantee that
  credentials are inaccessible or that nothing reaches the network.
- Only a session id that looks like one is kept and passed on.

### Added

- **Look things up online** (Agent): lets it search the web and open pages with Let it act
  off.

### Fixed

- Thinking effort works on opencode 2, which takes it on the model.

## [1.0.2] - 2026-11-05

### Fixed

- On Omarchy 4.5, where the bar's window spans the screen, the panel didn't open, or
  opened over the bar. It now opens off the bar's outer edge, on any edge and with any
  bar size.

## [1.0.1] - 2026-11-03

### Security

- Your question, the context sent with it and the answers no longer appear in command
  arguments, which other users on the computer can list. The agent gets the question on

- Let it act off is now enforced: opencode gets permissions that only let it read, search
  and look things up, so its Build agent can no longer edit files or run commands
  without asking.

### Changed

- The presets for your own command send the question on stdin (`claude -p`, `gemini`,
  `codex exec -`); the old presets are read the new way.

# Code of conduct

Pawmpt follows the [Contributor Covenant, version 2.1](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct/).

In short: be kind and patient, assume good intent, keep criticism about the work and
not the person, and leave out harassment of any kind. Issues, pull requests and
discussions that don't keep to this are closed.

To report something, open an issue or contact the maintainer through
[GitHub](https://github.com/qempexe).

# Contributing

Characters, skins and things to wear are welcome. Everyone taking part is expected to follow the [code of conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).

## A new character

1. Add a function to `shapes` in `qml/js/Draw.js`. It gets the canvas, the center, the ground line, the size, the breath and the options (`body`, `eye`, `accent`, `t`, `busy` and the rest listed at the top of the file), draws the body, and returns where the eyes go: `[{ x, y, r, square }]`. The eyes are drawn for you, blinking and looking around.
2. If it is shaped unlike the others, add its parts to `layouts` in the same file, so hats, glasses and patterns land in the right place.
3. Add `{ key, label, category }` to `characters` in `qml/js/Skins.js`.
4. Run `node tools/check.js`. It draws every character in every skin and with every item, at many sizes, and fails on broken numbers or drawings that leave the canvas.

## A new skin

Add `{ name, body, eye, accent }` to `presets` in `qml/js/Skins.js`. Keep the eyes readable on the body.

## Something to wear

Add it to `dressItems` in `qml/js/Skins.js` and its drawing to `dressDraw` in `qml/js/Draw.js`, then run the checks.

## A setting

Every setting lives in `qml/js/Schema.js`: its page, label, options and default. After adding one, run `node tools/gen-manifest.js` to update `manifest.json`.

## Checks

```bash
node tools/check.js            # every character, skin and item; the QML against Schema.js
node tests/test_manifest.js    # manifest.json against the code
node tests/test_prompt.js      # what is sent to the agent
node tests/test_voice.js       # voice input
node tests/test_glow.js        # the glow
node tests/test_bridges.js     # the agent bridges in tools/
python3 tests/test_bridge_common.py   # what the bridges share: key files, replies, stopping the agent
```

## Style

Modern JavaScript inside functions (`const`, `let`, arrow functions).

# Pawmpt agent approval bridge

Pawmpt can host an approval card for a custom agent adapter. The adapter owns the vendor's
permission protocol and translates it to these JSON Lines messages. The bridges for opencode,
Claude Code and Codex in this folder are such adapters, and `bridge_common.py` has what they
share.

Enable **Approval bridge** in Agent settings. Pawmpt starts the command with stdin open and sends
one line:

```json
{"pawmpt":"request","prompt":"the user's prompt","secrets":["*/.ssh/*","*.env"]}
```

`secrets` are Pawmpt's patterns for files that hold keys and passwords (shell-style, on the whole
path). An adapter should keep the agent from reading them where its agent can be told to.

When the agent needs approval, write this event to stdout:

```json
{"pawmpt":"permission","id":"request-id","title":"Run command?","detail":"git push origin main"}
```

Add `"allowAll":true` to offer **Allow all this run** as well; leave it out for a request that
should always be answered on its own. Pawmpt shows the title and detail as plain text, without
control and direction characters, and says so when a detail was too long to show in full. It then
sends one of these to the adapter's stdin:

```json
{"pawmpt":"permission_reply","id":"request-id","allow":true}
{"pawmpt":"permission_reply","id":"request-id","allow":false}
```

When **Allow all this run** was pressed, the first reply also has `"allowAll":true`, and every
waiting request that offered it gets an allow of its own. More than twelve requests waiting at
once are denied as they come.

The adapter should match replies by `id`, ignore a reply for an id it didn't ask about or already
has an answer for, keep the agent paused until the reply arrives, and translate the choice using
the agent's official API. Do not infer permission requests from ordinary assistant prose. Read
stdin in a thread or with non-blocking reads of your own: two replies can arrive in one write.

The adapter can also send:

```json
{"pawmpt":"text","text":"part of the answer"}
{"pawmpt":"activity","text":"› shell: git status"}
{"pawmpt":"usage","tokens":1234,"cost":0.0021}
{"pawmpt":"error","text":"what went wrong"}
```

`text` is added to the answer, `activity` is a step shown above it, `usage` is the tokens and
cost under it, and `error` ends the answer as a failure. Any other line on stdout is shown as part
of the answer.

Pawmpt keeps stdin open for replies. It stops the adapter with SIGTERM when you press Stop or the
time limit is reached, and closes stdin when it goes away itself: in both cases stop the agent and
everything it started, and treat every request still waiting as denied.
